value: Model-agnostic Python agent harness with MCP, multi-agent patterns, usage limits, and explicit timeout controls.
risk: Must be compatibility-tested with the chosen MCP SDK/version and local model endpoint before becoming runtime authority.
next_validation: Install in isolated environment; run a local stdio MCP smoke test and timeout/failure tests.

value: Open-weight-friendly second-engine candidate with tool calling, memory/RAG, code-interpreter examples, and MCP configuration support.
risk: Bundled code execution must not be treated as a production sandbox; model/tool compatibility needs a local test.
next_validation: Run Qwen-Agent against the same read-only MCP pack with an isolated local model and compare outputs independently.

value: Local OpenAI-compatible model endpoint with tool calling and no required cloud dependency for local inference.
risk: OpenAI compatibility is partial and model-specific tool quality varies.
next_validation: Detect an owned host with Ollama, start one tool-capable model, and run exact timeout/tool-call smoke tests.

value: A2A/MCP interop path that can expose an entire ADK agent as a standard MCP server.
risk: Adds another agent runtime; only useful if A2A or agent-as-MCP interoperability closes a real integration gap.
next_validation: Build one tiny agent-to-MCP example in isolation and measure whether it removes custom adapter code.

value: Local browser MCP path with configured allowed domains, sensitive-data masking, operation timeouts, and maximum step counts.
risk: Browser actions are externally stateful; allowlists and an independent approval/policy gate must be wired in front of the executor rather than merely documented.
next_validation: Run local MCP in a disposable profile with a single harmless allowlisted site and prove deny/approval behavior before broader use.

value: ByteDance multimodal GUI/browser stack with hybrid GUI/DOM browser control and an MCP-native kernel.
risk: High-authority computer-use surface; must be isolated from credentials, production sessions, and unrestricted filesystem/network access.
next_validation: Evaluate only in a disposable local desktop/browser profile behind the browser-policy MCP and explicit action approvals.

value: Git-backed memory filesystem with versioned Markdown memory, subagent worktrees, shared-memory repositories, and background memory maintenance.
risk: Agents can edit their own memory/context; direct self-mutation must not become execution or policy authority.
next_validation: Prototype a proposal-only memory lane where agent changes land on reviewable git refs and cannot alter runtime policy until independently admitted.

value: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway spanning many model providers plus A2A and MCP bridge/gateway functions.
risk: Central gateway can concentrate provider credentials and authority; not justified until there are multiple real backends to route.
next_validation: Defer deployment; when two model backends are live, test a loopback-only gateway with per-provider credentials and bounded MCP approval semantics.

value: Local open-source CLI/desktop/API agent with local Ollama support, MCP extensions, per-extension timeouts, and ACP providers.
risk: Built-in developer/computer-controller extensions have much broader authority than the narrow control-plane MCPs designed here.
next_validation: Test a custom goose distribution/session with only the read-only MCP pack enabled and all broad built-ins disabled.

value: Promising trust-layer memory approach surfaced through the MCP registry, designed around checking memory against filesystem/git before belief.
risk: Source, release provenance, write scope, and current exact version have not yet been independently verified in this program.
next_validation: Inspect current release/source/license, enumerate MCP tools and write permissions, and test stale-memory rejection on a disposable repository.

value: Research-grade verifiable memory with source-span citations, content hashes, HMAC anchoring, replay/tamper checks, and explicit threat-model caveats.
risk: Alpha research implementation; current store and agent share a process, so key extraction remains in threat model.
next_validation: Reproduce its deterministic citation/tamper tests locally and compare its provenance model with the existing content-addressed handoff design.

value: Local-first Markdown source-of-truth memory with SQLite FTS5 index, MCP transport, audit events, and federation/vector-clock concepts.
risk: Federated writable memory increases merge/authority complexity and requires source/release/security review before adoption.
next_validation: Inspect MCP mutation tools and prove an immutable/proposal-only mode can be enforced before considering integration.
